title: Plural and Third-Person S Endings (/s/, /z/, /ɪz/)
objectives: Determine ending sound based on preceding consonant voicing

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: Plural and Third-Person S Endings (/s/, /z/, /ɪz/). Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner adds extra syllable to 'books' (*book-iz).
💡 Solution: Teach rule: Only add extra syllable after hiss/buzz sibilant sounds.

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Plural and Third-Person S Endings (/s/, /z/, /ɪz/)
1. Definition: The suffix -s or -es has three distinct pronunciations conditioned by the final sound of the base word.
2. Rule: 1. After voiceless sound (/p, k, f, t/) = /s/ (cats). 2. After voiced sound (vowels, /b, g, v, d, m, n, l, r/) = /z/ (dogs). 3. After sibilants (/s, z, ʃ, tʃ, dʒ/) = /ɪz/ (buses, watches).
3. Why? Ease of articulation (assimilation of voicing).
4. How to recognize? Check the sound immediately before -s or -es.
5. Common examples: cats /kæts/, books /bʊks/, dogs /dɒgz/, pens /pɛnz/, buses /bʌsɪz/, watches /wɒtʃɪz/
6. Counter-examples: Irregular plurals (men, children).
7. Exceptions: house /haʊs/ -> houses /ˈhaʊzɪz/ (s becomes voiced /z/).
8. Common mistakes: Pronouncing /ɪz/ on every word (*cat-iz instead of cats).
9. Mnemonic / Hint: Sibilants get an EXTRA SYLLABLE /ɪz/! Unvoiced = /s/, Voiced = /z/!
10. Key vocabulary: sibilant, voiced, voiceless, plural, third-person -s, assimilation
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟢 A1
13. Associated Visual: 🔊 Voiced motor vs Voiceless whisper icon for S endings.
14. Key Takeaway: /s/ after unvoiced, /z/ after voiced, /ɪz/ after sibilants!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: How is 's' pronounced in 'cats' after unvoiced /t/? (/s/)
CCQ 2: How is 's' pronounced in 'dogs' after voiced /g/? (/z/)
CCQ 3: When does -es add an extra syllable /ɪz/? (After sibilant sounds like /s, z, ʃ, tʃ, dʒ/)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Classify the -s ending into /s/, /z/, or /ɪz/:
🎯 Item: books ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /s/ (after unvoiced /k/)
🎯 Item: dogs ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /z/ (after voiced /g/)
🎯 Item: buses ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: /ɪz/ (extra syllable after /s/)
